biography.plain_text: Charles Oswald Liddell was a British merchant who expanded a Shanghai wharf and trading business acquired through marriage to Elizabeth Birt. With his brother John, he developed Liddell Bros across several Chinese cities. He later settled at Shirenewton Hall in Wales and served as High Sheriff of Monmouthshire in 1918.

confidence.reason: Contemporary business ownership, independent auction histories, official estate history and the Gazette establish each factual component. The wording describes marital acquisition without claiming an exact legal instrument.

long_biography.plain_text:
Charles Oswald Liddell combined a trading career in China with a substantial collection of Chinese porcelain. He assembled it during decades abroad and worked with A. W. Bahr on a Shanghai exhibition in 1908. Part of his collection was offered by the London dealers Bluett & Sons in 1929, accompanied by a catalogue with 229 entries.

At Shirenewton Hall, his home in Wales, Liddell extended his collecting into the landscape. Chinese pavilions and a large bronze bell stood near the house, while a separate Japanese garden contained ponds, bridges, stone lanterns and a tea pavilion. He also gave the parish church an organ and a memorial bell.
